reasons: Directionally correct: the redline flips the default from Type II (IBM-owned) to Type I (Customer-owned) in p0082, so Materials created and paid for during the Services default to our ownership, matching the preferred position.

Rule-complete: it (i) confines Type II to IBM's pre-existing/generic IP, (ii) upgrades the licence-back to perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free with modification and sublicensing rights and removes the 'within Customer's Enterprise only' cap, including for Type II embedded in Type I deliverables, (iii) narrows IBM's licence in our Type I Materials to what is necessary to perform the Services (removing external distribution and the open-ended right to authorise 'others'), and (iv) adds an express Customer Content/Customer Components/data ownership and no-joint-ownership, no-assignment provision.
No residual assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM remains; IBM's retention of its own platform/pre-existing IP is preserved, which the rule permits.
Edits are targeted: p0082 is a one-word change; the higher change ratios in p0084/p0085 are justified because reversing the licence scope and re-defining Type II cannot be done with a smaller edit.

Comment is accurate to the cited text (Type II default, Enterprise-only licence, external distribution of our Materials), uses the [Playbook] prefix and required tone, and offers the fallback (IBM may keep generic tools/know-how if the broad licence-back and ownership confirmation stand).
